identify.note: Inputs are for the SEM on its own GNX USB link: 231D:2204 'VKBSim NXT SEM' (MobiFlight; with a THQ also attached 231D:2214 'VKBSim NXT SEM THQ', seen in a linux-hardware.org probe, SEM numbering unchanged). When the SEM is chained to a Gladiator stick it changes the stick's PID (e.g. 0204 'VKBsim Gladiator EVO R SEM' / 'VKBsim Gladiator NXT  R SEM', 0205 left) and its buttons move up by 40 (A1 = 41 ... SW1/SW2 report up, centre and down as separate buttons; the existing toggle entry was renamed to the 3-way vocabulary. devices.name: VKB Gladiator-K (Gladiator Mk.II / Pro base with Kosmosima space combat grip)

identify.note: 231D:0132 with HID name 'VKBsim Gladiator K' (manufacturer string 'VKB-Sim (C) Alex Oz 2023') from a linux-hardware.org USB probe. Pre-NXT Gladiator base with the first Kosmosima (SCG) grip: lockable MaRS twist, dual-action trigger, three gated 4-way hats with push, buttons (owners' reports; VKB's Kosmosima Standard spec lists 4 buttons). Factory button numbering not found, so the controls have no inputs. Base controls as on the Gladiator Mk.II / Pro (vkb-gladiator-mk2), numbering on this firmware unknown.

devices.name: VKB Gladiator Pro with MCG Pro grip ('Gladiator Modern Combat Pro')

identify.note: 231D:0131 with HID name 'VKBsim Gladiator Modern Combat Pro' (manufacturer string 'VKB-Sim Alex Oz 2021') from a linux-hardware.org USB probe. The MCG Pro grip on the pre-NXT Gladiator Pro base (VKB firmware 'Gl_MCG_MCG-Pro'; the Mamba w/ MCG Pro guide tells Gladiator Pro owners to load it). Grip controls as the Gunfighter MCG Pro (vkb-gunfighter-mcg-pro): dual-stage trigger, metal folding trigger, red weapon release, TMS/DMS/CMS 4-way hats with push, 8-way master-mode ministick, two analog ministicks, brake lever. Factory numbering on this base not found, so the controls have no inputs.

devices.name: VKB Black Mamba (Mamba joystick, 2014-2019; Long Mamba with extension)

identify.note: VKB Mamba base with the removable Mamba grip (Russian quick-start 2.2, 2014): Mamba grip with 2 ClusterFire triggers, 2 buttons, a pinky button, two 8-way hats and a 3-position mode switch; on the Black Mamba body only the aileron-trim encoder with push (front wall). Kits: Black Mamba (BM001), Long Mamba (LM001, with extension). The base also takes TM Warthog / Cougar grips (VKB adapter) and, from 2019, the VKB MCG Pro grip ('Mamba w/ MCG Pro'). NJoy32 controller; USB PID, HID name and DirectInput numbering not found (the manual lists controller line numbers, not button numbers), so the controls have no inputs.

devices.name: VKB Fat Mamba (Mamba joystick with switch-panel base, 2014; Long Fat Mamba / Maximum Mamba kits)

identify.note: Mamba base with the larger 'Fat' body (Russian quick-start 2.2, 2014; kits LFM001 Long Fat Mamba, MAXM001 Maximum Mamba with grip adapter). Body controls per the manual: 2 centre-detent potentiometers, 3 trim encoders with push (aileron, elevator, rudder), toggles and buttons named Batt, M1, M2, Gear, Flaps Up/Dn, Pump, Start, TMix Fw/Bck (5 two-position, 2 latched and 2 momentary three-position toggles, 1 button). Grip as the Black Mamba (vkb-black-mamba); also TM Warthog / Cougar grips via adapter. The manual gives NJoy32 line numbers only (e.g. Batt 9, M2 10, M1 11, Gear 12, Flaps Dn 13, Flaps Up 14, Pump 15, Start 16), not DirectInput numbers; USB PID and HID name not found, so no inputs. Which toggle is latched or momentary is not stated per control.

devices.name: VKB King Cobra USB (King Cobra Mk.I / Mk.II / Fat King Cobra, 2012-2015)

identify.note: 231D:0115 with HID name 'VKB KingCobra Fat #201' (manufacturer string 'www.vkb-sim.pro www.vkb-pro.ru Alex Oz 2013') from a linux-hardware.org USB probe of a Fat King Cobra; the user manual says Windows lists it as 'VKB King Cobra' plus the modification. VKB's metal-gimbal, MOForce-sensor joystick in the Defender Cobra M5 style body (manual 1.1, 2012): 3 axes (roll, pitch, throttle wheel), 2 ClusterFire triggers (main trigger and flip trigger, plus an auxiliary flip lever that presses both), 2 general buttons, a 4-way and an 8-way hat, a 3-position mode switch. Per the manual the two ClusterFire triggers are buttons 1 and 2 in every mode and every other button has three numbers, one per mode-switch position (7 physical buttons, 21 virtual); the exact numbers are not printed, so the other controls have no inputs. The King Cobra Mk.II Pro adds switch panels (panels.pdf).

devices.name: VKB T-Rudder Mk.I / Mk.II Pedals (no USB controller of their own)

identify.note: T-Rudder (manual 1.1, 2014) and T-Rudder Mk.II (quick start 1.1, 2015): single rudder axis (MaRS sensor on the Mk.II), no toe brakes and no onboard USB controller. They plug by RJ45 'RDR Link' into a Cobra-Z, a TinyBox or ThrottleBox controller, an NJoy32 Pro or the Gladiator's Pedals port and report through that device (on the Gladiator as RY). No USB id of their own.

devices.name: VKB T-Rudder Mk.III Pedals

identify.note: T-Rudder Mk.III (quick installation guide, 2015): single rudder axis, no toe brakes, its own USB connection plus an RDR Link port. USB PID and HID name not confirmed (the Mk.IV / Mk.V report 'VKBsim T-Rudder' on 231D:011F, see vkb-t-rudder-mk4); axis id not verified.

devices.name: VKB Mk.XXI Rudder Pedals (triple axis, toe brakes)

identify.note: Early VKB triple-axis rudder pedals (rudder plus two toe brakes), named in the Gladiator manual as a pedal unit for its Pedals port; VKB's FTP has 'Mk_XXI' pedal firmware (2015). On the Gladiator Pedals port they report as RY (rudder), RZ (left brake), Slider (right brake). Own USB id and HID name not found.

devices.name: VKB NJoy32 controller board (NJoy32 / NJoy32 Pro)

identify.note: VKB's 32-bit ARM USB HID joystick controller (the platform inside the Gladiator, Mamba, King Cobra, Cobra-Z conversion and later VKB devices), also sold as a board for DIY builds. Inputs are user-defined in VKBDevCfg (NJoy32 user guide 2.14-2.19); no fixed layout.

devices.name: VKB TinyBox (USB controller for VKB pedals)

identify.note: Small NJoy32-family USB controller that T-Rudder (Mk.I-Mk.IV) pedals connect to over RDR Link; pedals then report through the TinyBox (toe-brake axis combining is its default mode per the NJoy32 guide). Firmware 1.59-1.79 on VKB's FTP (2014-2016). USB id not found.

devices.name: VKB ThrottleBox (USB controller)

identify.note: NJoy32-family USB controller box (firmware 1.58, 2015) with a Pedals port for T-Rudder pedals; listed among the devices the NJoy32 configurator supports. Inputs depend on what is wired to it. USB id not found.

devices.name: VKB Gladiator NXT Omni Throttle (non-EVO NXT with OTA, SCG grip, right hand)

identify.note: 231D:3200 with HID name 'VKBsim Gladiator NXT OT R' (MobiFlight definition). The Gladiator NXT EVO Omni Throttle uses the same PID ('VKBsim Gladiator EVO OT R'), so the HID name tells them apart. Buttons 1-30 from the MobiFlight map, identical to the plain non-EVO NXT (vkb-gladiator-nxt): grip 1-22, NXT base EN1 23/24, EN2 25/26, F1-F3 27-29, A1 push 30. The A1 directions (POV1 on the EVO maps) are not in the MobiFlight map and have no input. The OTA turns the stick into an omnidirectional throttle; the throttle, twist and ministick axis ids were not verified for the non-EVO NXT (on the EVO OT the lever is JOY_Z), so those axes have no input. VKB's OTA is sold for NXT and EVO, left and right.

devices.name: VKB Gladiator NXT EVO Space Combat Edition Standard (left hand)

identify.note: Left-hand version of the Gladiator EVO 'Space Combat Edition' Standard (VKB-Sim AU sells right and left). SCG Standard grip: lockable MaRS twist, dual-action trigger, three 4-way hats with push, 4 buttons; no rapid-fire trigger and no analog ministick. USB PID / HID name and factory numbering for the Standard grip not found (the left SCG Premium on the EVO reports 231D:0201 'VKBsim Gladiator EVO L'), so the controls have no inputs; see vkb-gnx-evo-scg-standard for the right hand.

devices.name: VKB STECS Space Throttle Grip Max (right)

identify.note: Right-handed STECS Space Throttle System Max (STG-R grip, ATEM, STEM; VKB sells it as a variant of the Max). The left Max reports 231D:0139 and the right Mini / Mini Plus / Standard report 013A / 013B / 013C, but no source shows the right Max PID or HID name, and no numbered map for it was found, so the controls (copied from the left Max, vkb-stecs-stg-max-left) have no inputs.

devices.name: VKB KG12 GF (Gen.1) 'WWII Combat' grip for Gunfighter Mk.II/III

identify.note: First-generation KG12 grip for the Gunfighter Mk.II/III (not Mk.IV). Per VKB's product page: folding metal trigger, bomb release button, 4-way hat, profile-shift pinky button, lockable twist adapter (MaRS). The Gen.2 KG12 (vkb-gunfighter-kg12) has a paddle switch and ring-finger button instead. USB PID / HID name and numbering not found, so no inputs.

devices.name: Thrustmaster Warthog / Cougar / F16 / F18 grip on a VKB Gunfighter (VKB Warthog adapter)

identify.note: A Thrustmaster stick grip on a Gunfighter base through VKB's Thrustmaster / Warthog adapter (RevC for Mk.IV, older one for Mk.II/III; similar kits existed for the Gladiator Pro and the Black Mamba). The grip is read by the VKB controller, so it reports with VKB's USB id and VKB's numbering (VKB published 'BB_GF-TM' BlackBox profiles), not as a Thrustmaster device. USB PID / HID name and the numbering were not found, so the controls (Warthog names) have no inputs.
